- [2023/01/15] Vodou is still widely practiced in Haiti, with an estimated 60-80% of the population participating in some form of Vodou alongside Catholicism or Protestantism.
- [2023/01/15] Vodou serves as a source of resistance and community solidarity in Haiti, especially since the Haitian Revolution.
- [2023/01/15] Vodou plays a significant role in healing and trauma recovery in Haiti following natural disasters and political unrest.
- [2023/01/15] Vodou has spread beyond Haiti, with practitioners in the United States, Canada, France, Brazil, and various Caribbean countries.
- [2023/01/15] The practice and understanding of Vodou can vary significantly depending on cultural context and individual practitioners.
- [2023/01/15] Vodou is often misunderstood and misrepresented in popular culture, perpetuating harmful stereotypes and misconceptions.
- [2023/01/15] Misrepresentations of Vodou in media are partly due to the legacy of colonialism and slavery, which sought to demonize African and Afro-Caribbean spiritual practices.
